newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia cuts rates on pensioner savings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia cuts rates on pensioner savings.

text.p: The Australian government on Friday reduced the interest rates it deems pensioners to be receiving on their savings and investments by one percentage point, reflecting recent falls in official interest rates.
Social Security Minister Jocelyn Newman said the rate would be reduced to three percent for single pensioners with less than A$30,400 and couples with less than A$50,600.
The rate has been cut to five percent for retirees with more than those amounts. The cuts apply from September 20.

"Given the recent falls in official interest rates, combined with a low inflation environment, the government considers it is now an appropriate time to reassess the deeming rate," Newman said in a statement.

"The new deeming rates take into account reductions in official interest rates, the returns pensioners can obtain on bank, building society and credit union accounts, as well as the returns available on other financial investments such as shares and managed funds."
National Australia Bank (NAB) spokesman Haydn Park said the deeming rates had only fallen one percent in the time that the official cash rate had been reduced 2.5 percentage points, to 5.0 percent.
"The proper thing would be that it goes (down) at least 1.5 percent," he said.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia spokeswoman Lyndell Fraser said the deeming rate cut was not enough to make up for recent falls in official cash rates.
The government's decision not to declare the formula used to calculate the rate also left the bank and its customers in a difficult position, she said.
Fraser said CBA customers had about A$8.0 billion in these deeming accounts and the major banks overall had about A$18 billion in the accounts.
"It's a step in the right direction, however, official rates have moved 1.5 percent since the last reduction and the deeming rate has moved less than that," Fraser told Reuters.
"We still do not know the formula and that leaves our pensioner customers in a very difficult position in terms of knowing how to manage their assets," she said.
"At it leaves the bank in a similar position in terms of managing its balance sheet."
